title: Check what a chatbot says

cards.text: A chatbot can sound sure and still be wrong. AARP says chatbots can sound very confident even when an answer is wrong. Check important answers with a source you trust.
cards.line: A confident voice can still miss the mark.

cards.text: Do not type private details into a chatbot. AARP says to keep Social Security numbers, bank accounts, and passwords out of a chat.
cards.line: Keep private details out of the chat.

cards.text: AARP says to double-check chatbot answers, especially about health, money, or legal matters. Treat an answer as a starting point.
cards.line: Check the answer before you act.

checks.prompt: A chatbot gives advice about a health problem. What is the safer next step?
options: Share all your medical details with the chatbot
checks.why: AARP says chatbots can sound confident even when they are wrong. It says to double-check answers about health, money, or legal matters.

checks.prompt: Which detail should stay out of a chatbot?
options: A recipe idea for dinner today
A question about a book you are reading today
checks.why: AARP lists bank accounts and passwords as details to keep out of a chatbot.

checks.prompt: A chatbot sounds certain about a money choice. What should you do?
options: Ask the chatbot if it is sure
Ask the chatbot to explain every detail in a long reply
Check with a trusted source first
checks.answer: Check with a trusted source first
checks.why: AARP says to double-check answers about money and treat them as a starting point.

takeaway: Check important chatbot answers, and keep private details out.

sources.name: AARP, 6 ways to stay safe in a chatbot world
